annotations.title: Ask a person to do what a key can't

description: Open a request for a signed-in owner to connect a mailbox (kind connect_mailbox), replace the logins of one (kind update_mailbox_credentials, with its mailboxId), set up the bounce and complaint reports of a send-only mailbox (kind manage_report_hook, with its mailboxId: say in `note` whether to turn them on, give them a new secret or turn them off. The secret never reaches you, and a mailbox that has no reports to set up answers 409), approve a step of a copy of a mailbox's old mail to our servers (kind approve_mailbox_migration, with its mailboxId: the owner starts the copy, approves its folders or resumes it from the link. It answers 409 for a mailbox the copy isn't offered on, as preflight_mailbox_migration's `offered` says), send one lead anyway (kind send_lead_anyway, with its campaignId and the lead's contactId: say in `note` why you expect the address to get mail. Only a signed-in person who may send can say that an address gets mail, and no key can. The request is refused with 409 when the lead's address is on the suppression list, was found invalid, has a check still running, or the campaign already writes to it, and 404 for a lead that isn't in the campaign. That person sends it (the request completes, and the lead then shows `sendAnyway`) or declines (the request reads `cancelled`). A key an owner limited to other campaigns can't ask: 403 with `details.scope` keyCampaign), take a team action in Settings (kind manage_team: inviting, changing a role, removing a member or transferring ownership), choose a plan and pay for it (kind manage_billing: it completes when the owner opens the checkout or the billing portal; read the plan with get_billing, which changes only once Stripe confirms the payment. It is refused while get_billing says `available` is false or `changeVia` is `support`, since nobody could finish it), add or remove a mail domain (kind manage_mail_domains: say in `note` which name and which use. It completes when the owner adds or removes a domain from the link; read the result with list_mail_domains), create, change or delete a sender address (kind manage_sender_addresses: say in `note` which address and where replies should go. It completes when the owner makes, changes or deletes one from the link; read the result with get_sender_address and the handoff's resultMailboxId), or accept the acceptable use policy after a call was refused with AUP_REQUIRED (kind accept_aup; accepting completes every such request, and a workspace that already accepted answers 409). For a Microsoft 365 mailbox, the owner signs in with Microsoft instead of typing logins, and the same kinds apply. The answer carries a console link: give it to the person, then call get_handoff until status is completed. A request expires after 24 hours. A workspace opens at most 30 an hour. More person steps: confirm_mailbox_address takes mailboxId of a mailbox whose address is not confirmed yet (409 when it already is) and completes the moment the address is confirmed, by a code (typed by the owner or sent by a setup key), a Microsoft or Google sign-in, a verified mail domain or our staff. manage_tracking_domains opens Settings on tracking and completes when a signed-in owner or admin adds or removes a tracking domain. manage_webhook opens the webhook and completes after its owner saves or deletes it from the link. manage_settings opens the postal address and completes only after an owner or admin saves that address from the link, not a time-zone-only edit. These linked writes carry handoffId. add_dns_records takes exactly one of mailboxId (a connected mailbox's required SPF and DMARC, or DMARC alone for a send-only mailbox) and trackingDomainId (a tracking CNAME). Only our own fresh passing DNS read completes it, in the same transaction as the saved reading. No client claim, unanswered read or stale tracking write completes it. Several requests for that exact target can complete together. A key with a read list cannot ask about a workspace-wide tracking domain. No request grants authority or opens a hosted feature.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.
